Use the following data for this question.

SET 1 — NORTHRIDGE ELECTRONICS: Annual Revenue & Product Mix

Table 1 shows Northridge Electronics' total annual revenue, in millions of dollars, for the years 2019 through 2023. Bar Chart 1 shows each product category's share of total 2023 revenue, as a percentage of that total.

According to Table 1, what was Northridge Electronics' total revenue in 2021?

A. $96 million
B. $108 million
C. $120 million
D. $135 million
E. $150 million
questions.explanation: Direct read from Table 1: the 2021 row shows revenue = $108 million. No calculation needed.
questions.trap: Students glance at the row above or below and accidentally pick $96 million (2020) or $120 million (2019).

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

[SET 1 — NORTHRIDGE ELECTRONICS: Annual Revenue & Product Mix]

TABLE 1: Total Annual Revenue (in $ millions)
| Year | Revenue |
|------|---------|
| 2019 | 120     |
| 2020 | 96      |
| 2021 | 108     |
| 2022 | 135     |
| 2023 | 150     |

BAR CHART 1: Revenue Share by Product Category in 2023 (percent of total 2023 revenue)
| Category    | Share |
|-------------|-------|
| Smartphones | 40%   |
| Laptops     | 30%   |
| Accessories | 20%   |
| Smart Home  | 10%   |

Based on the data above, how much revenue, in millions of dollars, did the Laptops category generate in 2023?
questions.explanation: From Table 1, total 2023 revenue = $150 million. From Bar Chart 1, Laptops = 30% of total. Laptops revenue = 30% × $150M = 0.30 × 150 = $45 million.
questions.trap: Students use 30% of 2022 revenue ($135M) instead of 2023 revenue ($150M), getting $40.5M ≈ $40M (option B). The bar chart percentages apply to 2023 only.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 1 — NORTHRIDGE ELECTRONICS: Annual Revenue & Product Mix

Table 1 shows Northridge Electronics' total annual revenue, in millions of dollars, for the years 2019 through 2023. Bar Chart 1 shows each product category's share of total 2023 revenue, as a percentage of that total.

By what percentage did total revenue increase from 2020 to 2022? Enter your answer to the nearest whole number percent.
questions.explanation:
Revenue in 2020 = $96M; Revenue in 2022 = $135M.
Percent change = (New − Old) / Old × 100 = (135 − 96) / 96 × 100 = 39/96 × 100 = 40.625% ≈ 41%.
The question asks to the nearest whole number, so the answer is 41.
questions.trap: Students compute (135 − 96)/135 × 100 = 28.9% ≈ 29%, dividing by the NEW value (2022) instead of the ORIGINAL value (2020). Percent change always uses the original as the base.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 1 — NORTHRIDGE ELECTRONICS: Annual Revenue & Product Mix

Table 1 shows Northridge Electronics' total annual revenue, in millions of dollars, for the years 2019 through 2023. Bar Chart 1 shows each product category's share of total 2023 revenue, as a percentage of that total.

Quantity A: Smartphones revenue in 2023 (in $ millions)
Quantity B: Total revenue in 2019 (in $ millions)
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Quantity A: Smartphones = 40% of 2023 total = 0.40 × $150M = $60M.
Quantity B: 2019 total revenue = $120M.
$60M < $120M, so Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Students may misread the bar chart and use Laptops (30%) rather than Smartphones (40%) for Quantity A, computing $45M, which still gives B > A — but for the wrong reason. The correct calculation is 40% × $150M = $60M.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

According to the Line Graph, in which year was total enrollment the lowest?

A. 2018
B. 2019
C. 2020
D. 2021
E. 2022
questions.explanation:
Reading the Line Graph:
2018: 42,000 — the lowest value among all six years listed.
2019: 45,000; 2020: 43,000; 2021: 47,000; 2022: 50,000; 2023: 52,000.
The minimum is 42,000 in 2018.
questions.trap: Students notice 2020 (43,000) is lower than 2019 (45,000) and pick 2020, missing that 2018 (42,000) is even lower. Always check all data points when asked for a minimum.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

Approximately how many students were enrolled at the Middle School level in 2023?

A. 10,500
B. 12,500
C. 13,000
D. 15,600
E. 23,400
questions.explanation:
From the Line Graph, total 2023 enrollment = 52,000 students.
From the Pie Chart, Middle School = 25% of total.
Middle School enrollment = 25% × 52,000 = 0.25 × 52,000 = 13,000 students.
questions.trap: Students use 2022 enrollment (50,000) from the line graph instead of 2023 (52,000), computing 25% × 50,000 = 12,500 (option B). Always confirm which year's data the question references.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

Quantity A: Number of High School students enrolled in 2023
Quantity B: Number of Elementary students enrolled in 2021
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Quantity A: High School in 2023 = 30% × 52,000 = 15,600 students.
Quantity B: Elementary students in 2021 — the Pie Chart only gives the 2023 breakdown. We do not have the 2021 breakdown by level. We only know total 2021 enrollment = 47,000. Without the 2021 level percentages, Quantity B cannot be determined.
Therefore, the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Students apply the 2023 pie chart percentages to 2021 enrollment, computing 45% × 47,000 = 21,150 and concluding Quantity B is greater. The pie chart percentages apply ONLY to 2023 — we cannot assume the same distribution for 2021.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

The number of Elementary School students in 2023 was how many more than the number of High School students in 2023? Enter your answer in whole number of students.
questions.explanation:
Total 2023 enrollment = 52,000 students.
Elementary = 45% × 52,000 = 23,400 students.
High School = 30% × 52,000 = 15,600 students.
Difference = 23,400 − 15,600 = 7,800 students.
questions.trap: Students compute the difference in percentages (45% − 30% = 15%) and report 15,000 or 15% without multiplying by the actual total. The percentage difference must be applied to the real enrollment figure.

SET 3 — RIVER COUNTY POPULATION STUDY

Table 2 shows the population of each of four cities, in thousands, in 2015, 2020, and 2023. Bar Chart 2 shows the percentage of each city's 2023 population that was aged 65 or older.

Approximately how many residents aged 65 or older lived in Brentville in 2023?

A. 20,400
B. 25,200
C. 26,400
D. 30,000
E. 33,000
questions.explanation:
From Table 2, Brentville's 2023 population = 132,000.
From Bar Chart 2, Brentville has 20% aged 65+.
Residents aged 65+ = 20% × 132,000 = 0.20 × 132,000 = 26,400.
questions.trap: Students use Brentville's 2020 population (126,000) instead of 2023 (132,000), computing 20% × 126,000 = 25,200 (option B). The 65+ percentages shown in the bar chart correspond to 2023 populations.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 3 — RIVER COUNTY POPULATION STUDY

Table 2 shows the population of each of four cities, in thousands, in 2015, 2020, and 2023. Bar Chart 2 shows the percentage of each city's 2023 population that was aged 65 or older.

Which of the following cities in the absolute number of residents aged 65+ in 2023 exceeded 14,000?

Select all that apply.

A. Alderton
B. Brentville
C. Clarksburg
D. Dunmore
questions.explanation:
Calculate 65+ count for each city using 2023 populations:
- Alderton: 15% × 96,000 = 14,400 > 14,000 ✓
- Brentville: 20% × 132,000 = 26,400 > 14,000 ✓
- Clarksburg: 12% × 78,000 = 9,360 < 14,000 ✗
- Dunmore: 25% × 40,000 = 10,000 < 14,000 ✗

Although Dunmore has the highest percentage (25%), its small total population makes the absolute count only 10,000. Cities A and B qualify.
questions.trap: Students select Dunmore (D) because it has the highest percentage (25%), not realizing that 25% of a small population (40,000) yields only 10,000 residents — less than the 14,000 threshold. Absolute count = percentage × base, and the base matters.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 3 — RIVER COUNTY POPULATION STUDY

Table 2 shows the population of each of four cities, in thousands, in 2015, 2020, and 2023. Bar Chart 2 shows the percentage of each city's 2023 population that was aged 65 or older.

Quantity A: Percent population growth of Clarksburg from 2015 to 2023
Quantity B: Percent population growth of Alderton from 2015 to 2023
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.trap: Students compare absolute growth (Clarksburg +18 thousand versus Alderton +16 thousand) or divide by the 2023 population instead of the 2015 base.

Use the following data for this question:

SET 4 - NATIONAL BASKETBALL LEAGUE STATS: Team Performance

Table 3 below shows the season records for selected teams. The line graph below shows the Eagles' monthly win totals from October through March.

According to Table 3, which team had the highest average points scored per game?

A. Eagles
B. Wolves
C. Panthers
D. Ravens
E. Eagles and Wolves tied
questions.explanation:
Direct read from the 'Points For' column in Table 3:
- Eagles: 112
- Wolves: 108
- Panthers: 104
- Ravens: 98
The highest average is 112 (Eagles).
questions.trap: Students confuse 'Points For' (scored by the team) with 'Points Against' (scored by opponents). They might pick Ravens because 114 is the highest value visible in the table — but 114 is the points scored AGAINST Ravens, not by them.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 4 - NATIONAL BASKETBALL LEAGUE STATS: Team Performance

Table 3 below shows the season records for selected teams. The line graph below shows the Eagles' monthly win totals from October through March.

Which of the following months in the Eagles' win total was strictly above the team's average monthly wins for the season?

Select all that apply.

A. October
B. November
C. December
D. January
E. February
questions.explanation:
From the Line Graph, Eagles' total wins = 6+10+9+11+9+9 = 54 (consistent with Table 3).
Months = 6, so average monthly wins = 54 ÷ 6 = 9.0.

Months STRICTLY above 9:
- October: 6 < 9 ✗
- November: 10 > 9 ✓
- December: 9 = 9 ✗ (not strictly above)
- January: 11 > 9 ✓
- February: 9 = 9 ✗ (not strictly above)
- March: 9 = 9 ✗

Only November and January exceed the average.
questions.trap: Students include December, February, and March because they are 'at or above' average, missing the word 'strictly.' The question says strictly above, which excludes months equal to the mean (9). Only months with more than 9 wins qualify.

SET 5 - METROPOLITAN RETAIL GROUP: Sales Analysis

Bar Chart 3 below shows quarterly revenue by region in 2023, in millions of dollars. Pie Chart 2 gives the full-year 2023 revenue breakdown by product type, as a percentage of the company's $670 million full-year total; its slice values are listed in the accompanying table.

According to Bar Chart 3, which region had the highest Q1 revenue?

A. North
B. South
C. East
D. West
E. North and South tied
questions.explanation:
Q1 values from Bar Chart 3:
- North: $40M
- South: $30M
- East: $25M
- West: $20M
Highest Q1 revenue: North at $40M.
questions.trap: Students look at Q4 values (the largest figures overall) instead of Q1, and pick North based on Q4's $60M. The question specifies Q1 specifically.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 5 - METROPOLITAN RETAIL GROUP: Sales Analysis

Bar Chart 3 below shows quarterly revenue by region in 2023, in millions of dollars. Pie Chart 2 gives the full-year 2023 revenue breakdown by product type, as a percentage of the company's $670 million full-year total; its slice values are listed in the accompanying table.

Approximately how much revenue (in $ millions) did Electronics generate in full-year 2023?

A. $140.0M
B. $162.4M
C. $175.8M
D. $187.6M
E. $234.5M
questions.explanation:
The Pie Chart states the total 2023 revenue = $670M.
Electronics share = 28%.
Electronics revenue = 28% × $670M = 0.28 × 670 = $187.6M.
questions.trap: Students compute the total from Bar Chart 3: (40+45+50+60) + (30+35+40+45) + (25+30+35+30) + (20+25+30+35) = 195+150+120+110 = $575M, then compute 28% × $575M = $161M ≈ $162M (option B). The bar chart only shows 4 regions but the pie chart states the full-year total is $670M — a different (higher) base that includes all regions.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 5 - METROPOLITAN RETAIL GROUP: Sales Analysis

Bar Chart 3 below shows quarterly revenue by region in 2023, in millions of dollars. Pie Chart 2 gives the full-year 2023 revenue breakdown by product type, as a percentage of the company's $670 million full-year total; its slice values are listed in the accompanying table.

The North region's annual revenue in 2023 represented approximately what percentage of the full-year company revenue? Round your answer to the nearest tenth of a percent (e. g., 12.3).
questions.explanation:
North region annual revenue = sum of all quarters = 40 + 45 + 50 + 60 = $195M.
Full-year company revenue = $670M (stated in Pie Chart).
Percentage = 195/670 × 100 = 29.104...% ≈ 29.1%.
questions.trap: Students use only one quarter (60/670 ≈ 9.0%), or leave the answer as a decimal (0.291) instead of a percent.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 5 - METROPOLITAN RETAIL GROUP: Sales Analysis

Bar Chart 3 below shows quarterly revenue by region in 2023, in millions of dollars. Pie Chart 2 gives the full-year 2023 revenue breakdown by product type, as a percentage of the company's $670 million full-year total; its slice values are listed in the accompanying table.

Quantity A: Revenue from Clothing product type in full-year 2023
Quantity B: Combined annual revenue of the South and East regions in 2023
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Quantity A: Clothing = 35% × $670M = $234.5M.
Quantity B: South = 30+35+40+45 = $150M; East = 25+30+35+30 = $120M; combined = $270M.
$234.5M < $270M, so Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Students compare Quantity A with the South region alone ($150M) and conclude Quantity A is greater, or compute 35% of the wrong total.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 6 - COUNTY HOSPITAL NETWORK: Patient & Cost Data

Table 4 below shows annual patient admissions by department. Line Graph 2 below shows the average cost per admission, in dollars, by year.

Which department had the greatest total number of patient admissions across all four years (2020–2023)?

A. Cardiology
B. Orthopedics
C. Neurology
D. General Surgery
E. Pediatrics
questions.explanation:
Sum of all four years per department:
- Cardiology: 4,800+5,100+5,400+5,700 = 21,000
- Orthopedics: 3,200+3,400+3,600+3,800 = 14,000
- Neurology: 2,100+2,300+2,500+2,400 = 9,300
- General Surgery: 6,500+6,200+6,800+7,200 = 26,700
- Pediatrics: 4,400+4,600+4,500+4,700 = 18,200
Largest total: General Surgery at 26,700.
questions.trap: Students look only at 2023 values (the most recent year) and may compare Cardiology (5,700) vs General Surgery (7,200) without summing all years. For cumulative totals, all rows must be added — General Surgery consistently dominates.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 6 - COUNTY HOSPITAL NETWORK: Patient & Cost Data

Table 4 below shows annual patient admissions by department. Line Graph 2 below shows the average cost per admission, in dollars, by year.

Approximately what was the total revenue generated by the Cardiology department in 2023? Enter your answer in millions of dollars, rounded to the nearest tenth (e.g., 57.0).
questions.explanation:
Cardiology admissions in 2023 = 5,700 (from Table 4).
Average cost per admission in 2023 = $10,000 (from Line Graph 2).
Total revenue = 5,700 × $10,000 = $57,000,000 = $57.0 million.
questions.trap: Students use the 2022 cost per admission ($9,200) with 2023 admissions, computing 5,700 × $9,200 = $52.44M — mixing data from different years. Each question about a specific year requires using that year's cost figure from the line graph AND that year's admissions from the table.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 6 - COUNTY HOSPITAL NETWORK: Patient & Cost Data

Table 4 below shows annual patient admissions by department. Line Graph 2 below shows the average cost per admission, in dollars, by year.

Quantity A: Percent change in Neurology admissions from 2021 to 2023
Quantity B: Percent change in average cost per admission from 2021 to 2023
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.trap: Students compare absolute changes: Quantity A is 2,400−2,300 = 100 and Quantity B is 10,000−8,500 = 1,500, then conclude B is obviously larger — which happens to give the right answer for the wrong reason. The question tests percent change, not absolute change. For QC percent-change problems, always divide by the original.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 7 — CITY OF LAKEWOOD: Demographics & Housing

Table 5 shows Population by District (in thousands) for 2010, 2015 and 2020.
Pie Chart 3 shows the 2020 Housing Type Distribution as a percentage of all housing units in Lakewood. Total housing units in 2020: 125,000.

Which of the following districts had a population in 2020 greater than 20 percent of the total city population in 2020?

Indicate all such districts.

A. Downtown
B. Midtown
C. Northshore
D. Eastside
E. Southgate
questions.explanation:
Total 2020 population = 290,000. The 20% threshold = 0.20 × 290,000 = 58,000.
- Downtown: 58,000 — exactly at 20%, does NOT exceed ✗
- Midtown: 72,000 > 58,000 ✓
- Northshore: 60,000 > 58,000 ✓
- Eastside: 50,000 < 58,000 ✗
- Southgate: 50,000 < 58,000 ✗
Only Midtown (B) and Northshore (C) strictly exceed 20% of the total.
questions.trap: Students include Downtown (A) because 58,000 = 20% — they misread 'exceeded' as 'equaled or exceeded.' The word 'exceeded' means strictly greater than, so Downtown, at exactly 20%, does not qualify.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 7 — CITY OF LAKEWOOD: Demographics & Housing

Table 5 shows Population by District (in thousands) for 2010, 2015 and 2020.
Pie Chart 3 shows the 2020 Housing Type Distribution as a percentage of all housing units in Lakewood. Total housing units in 2020: 125,000.

In 2020, how many persons per housing unit were there in Lakewood, on average? Round your answer to the nearest hundredth (e. g., 2.35).
questions.explanation:
Total population in 2020 = 290,000 (from Table 5 TOTAL row).
Total housing units in 2020 = 125,000 (from Pie Chart note).
Persons per unit = 290,000 / 125,000 = 2.32.
questions.trap: Students use 2015 population (260,000) divided by 125,000 = 2.08, mixing years. Or they use the pie chart percentages to compute something unrelated. The population figure must come from the 2020 TOTAL row in Table 5, and the housing unit figure comes from the pie chart note — two different data sources combined correctly.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question:

SET 8 — BRANDFORD UNIVERSITY: Research Funding & Output

Bar Chart 4 shows Annual Research Grants Received by Department (in $ millions) for 2019 through 2023.
The table below (Line Graph 3) shows Annual Published Research Papers, all departments combined.

Quantity A: Percentage increase in total grants (all departments) from 2019 to 2023
Quantity B: Percentage increase in total papers published from 2019 to 2023
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.trap: Students compare the absolute increases: Quantity A increased by $36M and Quantity B by 140 papers. Since the units differ and 140 > 36, students may incorrectly choose B. The question asks for PERCENTAGE increases, not absolute increases. The percent calculation requires dividing by the original value in each case.
